title: A Provision for the Escarpment
premise: Elodie Eastwick, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Verrin brothers—cheerful lenders who collect in blood—finds a sealed chest washed out of a collapsed riverbank, stamped with the crest of Kessavia, a nation erased from maps a century ago. Inside are coordinates and a ledger promising an inheritance claim that could clear his debts or bury him. Pursued by the Verrins, a rival salvage crew, and a government archivist who knows too much, Elodie leads a ragtag expedition up the escarpment to verify the claim before the legal window closes at winter's first snow. He reaches the summit vault and discovers the 'inheritance' is a poisoned trust: whoever claims it inherits the dead nation's crimes and its surviving enemies. In the end Elodie burns the ledger publicly, pays the Verrins with the only thing left—the chest itself, which they wanted all along—and walks away owing nothing but the truth he'll never tell.
about_author: Emrys Hartwell is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent eleven years mapping floodplains across three continents before turning to fiction. Hartwell writes adventure novels from a houseboat that changes ports every season, claiming that staying still is how stories die.

chapters.title: The Optimists' Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Elodie Eastwick, POV. A tornado chase goes wrong and Elodie totals his truck, deepening his debt to the unfailingly cheerful Verrin brothers, who give him thirty days. The chapter establishes his skill, his recklessness, and the warm menace of his creditors. Emotional beat: dread wearing a smile.

chapters.title: What the River Surrenders
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Surveying flood damage for insurance money, he spots a chest exposed in a collapsed bank and pries it open: Kessavian seal, coordinates, a wax-protected ledger naming an heir. He pockets it against every instinct. Emotional beat: greed and wonder arriving together, unwelcome guests.

chapters.title: A Dead Nation's Signature
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Researching Kessavia in a university archive, he learns the nation was dissolved after a scandal its records were burned to hide—and that the ledger's legal window closes at first snow. An archivist, Maren Kolb, notices his questions. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into being watched.

chapters.title: Terms of Collection
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. The Verrins learn of the chest through a dock informant and offer to fund an expedition—for sixty percent and total disclosure. Elodie lies about what the ledger says. Emotional beat: the specific nausea of lying to people who enjoy catching liars.

chapters.title: Crew of the Desperate
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. He assembles a team: disgraced guide Tomas Reyes, explosives-savvy cook Petra Ilves, and Maren, who invites herself and won't say why. Each has a reason to need this trip more than safety. Emotional beat: camaraderie built on shared secrets, already cracking.

chapters.title: Departure at High Water
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. The expedition launches upriver as autumn storms build. Maren reveals she knows the ledger is one of three copies and doesn't trust Elodie's. Tension between them sharpens into wary alliance. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's craftsmanship.

chapters.title: The Salvage Crew
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. A rival boat shadows them—Harrow & Finch Salvage, hired by someone who knew the route before Elodie did. A night collision costs them fuel and nearly Petra. Emotional beat: the realization that the leak was inside the crew.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Petra confesses she sold their route to Harrow & Finch to buy her brother's freedom from a mining contract—but insists she never mentioned the ledger. Elodie must decide whether to maroon her or use her guilt. Emotional beat: mercy as a calculated investment.

chapters.title: The Escarpment's Teeth
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. The river ends; the climb begins. Switchbacks, rockfall, and the first snow dusting the heights compress their timeline brutally. Tomas breaks his wrist saving Maren. Emotional beat: the wilderness collecting its toll in bone, indifferent to deadlines.

chapters.title: Verrin Country
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. The Verrins' advance man catches up with supplies and a message: they know about the second ledger copy, and the discount for honesty expires soon. Elodie realizes the brothers funded Harrow & Finch too—betting both sides. Emotional beat: understanding that his creditors never expected repayment in money.

chapters.title: The Waystation Ghosts
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. They shelter in an abandoned Kessavian waystation, walls covered in refugees' chalk messages from a century ago. Petra finds a child's drawing of the vault door. Emotional beat: grief for strangers, and the first hint that the inheritance is not treasure.

chapters.title: Harrow's Offer
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Finch of Harrow & Finch corners Elodie alone and offers to buy him out entirely—generously—if he abandons the claim. Elodie realizes Finch believes the vault holds something worse than gold. Emotional beat: temptation that smells like fear.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. A blizzard pins them for two days above the treeline. Rations fail; Maren reveals her secret—her grandfather signed the dissolution order and she needs proof of what was hidden to redeem the family name. Emotional beat: confession as survival, warmth found in shared ruin.

chapters.title: The Second Copy
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. They find evidence someone reached the escarpment decades ago and died short of the vault—with a second ledger copy, water-damaged but legible, showing the coordinates differ slightly from Elodie's. Someone altered the first copy. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under everything he trusted.

chapters.title: Which Liar Led Us Here
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Accusations fly: Elodie's copy may be the forgery, planted by the Verrins to send expendable debtors up the mountain. Tomas turns back with the injured rather than follow a possibly false map. Emotional beat: the expedition fracturing along the fault line of trust.

chapters.title: The Vault Door
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Using both ledgers' discrepancy, Elodie triangulates the true entrance—a carved Kessavian seal half-buried in scree. Petra's charges open it as the sky clears and the temperature plummets. Emotional beat: awe immediately shadowed by the certainty that doors this well-hidden were hidden for reasons.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Ash
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Inside: no gold. The vault holds proof that Kessavia's ruling family engineered the disaster that destroyed them, blaming a neighbor nation—and documents valuable enough that several governments would kill to own or bury them. The 'heir' inherits culpability, not wealth. Emotional beat: horror dressed as vindication.

chapters.title: Everyone Arrives
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. The Verrins, Finch, and the survivors converge at the vault mouth as snow begins in earnest. Guns come out; everyone wants the documents, and Elodie stands between them holding the only complete set. Emotional beat: the eye of the storm, everyone calculating, no one breathing.

chapters.title: The Price Quoted
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. The Verrins offer Elodie his freedom for the documents; Finch offers more; Maren offers truth. Elodie understands any sale makes him complicit in whatever comes next. He asks for matches instead of money. Emotional beat: clarity arriving at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: First Snow
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Elodie burns the documents in the vault doorway, declaring the inheritance refused on behalf of a nation that no longer exists to refuse it. Chaos erupts; Petra and Maren drag him clear as the blizzard swallows the mountain. Emotional beat: liberation and loss igniting in the same flame.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Downriver, the Verrins take the empty chest—which, Elodie reveals, contains the Kessavian seal itself, worth fortunes to collectors—and call the debt settled, cheerful as ever. Finch retreats; Maren publishes only the refugees' chalk messages, history without ammunition. Emotional beat: exhaustion mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: What the Wilderness Remembers
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Spring. Elodie, debt-free and deliberately poor, chases storms again but keeps a chalk stub in his pocket. When Maren sends a postcard asking if he regrets burning it, he writes back: the mountain kept what mattered. Emotional beat: quiet absolution, and the knowledge that some provisions are made by refusing them.
